title: Decision Practice
subtitle: Stop & Decide prompts to build active clinical judgment
howToUse: These decision points interrupt passive reading and force active thinking. For each scenario, pause and write your response. Then compare with the model response. Focus on (1) the immediate risk, (2) the safest first nursing action, and (3) what data you must check next.

decisions.title: Oxygenation drop (ABCs)
decisions.scenario: A patient scheduled for surgery is sitting in bed reviewing the consent form. During conversation, the patient states, “I signed this because they told me to, but I don’t really understand what they’re going to do.” The patient appears anxious and hesitant when asked about the procedure.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Stop the process and notify the provider.

decisions.title: Patient refusal of care
decisions.scenario: A fully alert and oriented patient refuses a prescribed treatment, stating they do not want it administered. The patient understands the explanation provided but clearly states they are choosing not to proceed.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Respect the refusal and document appropriately.
decisions.modelWhy: Patients have the right to refuse care.

decisions.title: Confidentiality breach
decisions.scenario: While riding in a hospital elevator, a nurse overhears another staff member discussing a patient’s diagnosis and treatment details aloud, with visitors present nearby.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Scope of practice
decisions.scenario: A colleague asks you to perform a clinical task that is outside your authorised scope of practice, explaining that they are busy and “it will only take a minute.”
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Delegation to UAP
decisions.scenario: You are caring for multiple patients and consider delegating the task of taking routine vital signs for a stable patient to an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP).
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Unsafe assignment
decisions.scenario: At the start of your shift, you are assigned a patient load that exceeds safe staffing levels. You feel that providing safe, quality care to all assigned patients may not be possible.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Communicate concerns to the charge nurse.

decisions.title: Medication error disclosure
decisions.scenario: After reviewing medication records, you realise that a patient received an incorrect medication dose earlier in the shift. The patient has not yet shown any signs of harm.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: End-of-life decision
decisions.scenario: A terminally ill patient clearly expresses the wish to focus on comfort measures only and decline further aggressive treatment. Family members appear distressed by the patient’s decision.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
